model_output.cross_horizon_summary: The evidence supports no clear 12h directional edge, a low-confidence downside bias over 72h, and no reliable net direction over 168h. Positive 24h participation conflicts with weaker hourly prices, fading breadth, negative BTC settled ETF flows and contracting stablecoin supply. Cross-cap participation is observable only through proxies; persistent altcoin transmission is not confirmed. These are non-binding descriptive forecasts, not execution permissions or changes to framework rules. The structural prior is context, not an independent confirming vote.
global_missing_evidence: The packet supplies one completed hourly candle per pair, not a price-and-volume sequence sufficient to establish persistence or reliable technical levels.
Canonical large-cap and broad-alt breadth remain unconfirmed. Breadth aggregates and capitalization buckets share the same upstream family and must not be counted as independent confirmations.
The small-alt proxy covers only the Top-100 tail; the broader small-cap universe and microcaps are unobserved.
BTC dominance is one settled daily observation, not an intraday reading or a demonstrated trend. Current ETH/BTC also lacks a supplied comparison sequence.
The latest settled ETF session is October 23. The packet does not provide newer settled flows or the underlying multi-session series needed to verify continuation.
Stablecoin supply does not establish exchange inflows or capital deployment. Deployment confirmation is explicitly not established.

Catalyst context is degraded, macro observations have different lags, and derivatives lack historical positioning and funding baselines. These limitations reduce confidence rather than constitute bearish evidence.
